chunks: And Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Hashim Dawud ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari who said:

I was imprisoned with Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the prison of al-Muhtadi ibn al-Wathiq. He said to me: 'O Abu Hashim, this transgressor wanted to play with divine destiny in this night. And Allah, the Exalted, has cut off his life, and He has made his kingdom for the Qa'im who will come after him. I do not have a son yet, but I will be bestowed with a son.' Abu Hashim said: 'So when we woke up and the sun rose, the Turks attacked al-Muhtadi and killed him, and al-Mu'tamid succeeded him in his place, and Allah saved us.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s) predict about the Abbasid caliphs and his own family?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Imam’s awareness of contemporary political shifts, specifically the swift death of Caliph al-Muhtadi and the rise of al-Mu'tamid, as signs of divine will. It connects these historical events to the imminent birth of Imam al-Mahdi (a.j.), emphasizing that the 'tyrant's' interference was merely a prelude to the establishment of the Qa'im's authority. The narrative underscores the Shia belief in the Imam's occultation preparation and the transition of power from the Abbasids to the Ahl al-Bayt.
